posts.title: Warren McCulloch, chairman [sic] of the Macy Conferences on Cybernetics, in a letter to the cybernetics group before the tenth and final conference, 1953. Discovered and shared by Sean Manion.
posts.summary: A route to an image of a McCulloch letter associated with the final Macy conference. The image attribution and historical context require archival verification before any new lineage claim.

posts.title: BI 247 Maxim Raginsky: A Control Theory View on Brains and AI
posts.summary: A Brain Inspired conversation with Maxim Raginsky about control theory, brains and artificial intelligence. Inclusion identifies the episode rather than validating each argument in it.
posts.duplicate_reason: The identical Brain Inspired episode was already recorded on 7 October; this is a repeat announcement.

posts.title: Love & Philosophy – Andrea Hiott
posts.summary: Andrea Hiott’s Love & Philosophy podcast collection, offering a route into philosophical conversations. Individual episodes and their claims require their own review.

posts.title: #95 Inventing Temperature, Operational Coherence, Activist Realism and Active Knowledge with Cambridge philosopher Hasok Chang
posts.summary: A Love & Philosophy conversation with Hasok Chang about temperature, operational coherence and scientific knowledge. This is a specific episode, distinct from the wider podcast collection.

posts.title: Call for Thematic Sessions – – FedCSIS 2027
posts.summary: A call for proposed thematic sessions at FedCSIS 2027. The accessible lead does not establish a dated, bookable session, so it remains reading and announcement material.

posts.title: Design Horizon – An open library of emerging practices and provocations for tackling our world’s most wicked problems – Guerra (2026)
posts.summary: Design Horizon already has an attributed reading route with eight selected resources.
posts.duplicate_reason: Design Horizon already has an attributed reading route with eight selected resources.

posts.title: Our minds aren’t equipped to handle AI
posts.summary: An article considering how people understand and use artificial intelligence. This records a public discussion lead, without adopting its psychological claims as established atlas evidence.

posts.title: Doing Serious Systems Thinking Means Getting Rid of Elephants, Icebergs and Leverage Points – Jackson (2026) on LinkedIn
posts.summary: Michael C. Jackson’s critique of common systems-thinking metaphors and intervention shortcuts. The critical argument remains attributed to Jackson and can be compared with the approaches he discusses.

posts.title: Nonchaotic model reveals how predictability can emerge from seemingly unpredictable dynamics by Daniel Inafuku
posts.summary: A science-news account of research on predictable patterns in nonchaotic dynamics. Follow its cited research before treating the report as evidence for a general claim about complex systems.

posts.title: 42 | The Systemic Review- a publication of SCiO
posts.summary: A SCiO publication offering analyses of public problems through systems principles. Its papers and editorial account are linked as a collection; individual policy claims remain separately assessable.

posts.title: Unstable systems demand fast reflexes
posts.summary: A systems essay about response speed in unstable systems. Compare its argument with specified disturbances, delays and stability conditions rather than inferring a universal management rule.

posts.title: Richard S O’Rourke – Two entropies, two cornerstones
posts.summary: Richard S O’Rourke’s writing connects questions in thermodynamics, cybernetics and political economy. This route preserves the author’s account without equating distinct uses of entropy.

posts.title: The Strategy Dynamics Insights Library
posts.summary: A library of Strategy Dynamics articles and practical explanations. The collection is a learning route; its size or presence does not establish the effectiveness of every application.

posts.title: What’s in a name? From Norbert Wiener’s Teleology to Artificial Intelligence
posts.summary: A SCiO resource examining the terminology connecting Wiener’s teleology and artificial intelligence. Historical and conceptual claims remain attributable to the resource and need passage-level review.

posts.title: Modelling Prevention Policy Impacts on Local Authority-Funded Social Care Services in England: A System Dynamics Modelling Approach
posts.summary: An Applied Sciences paper applying system dynamics to prevention and local-authority-funded social care in England. Publication and modelling scope are recorded without treating simulated outcomes as observed policy effects.

posts.title: AI Agents Gone Wild, and the Dangers of Inference
posts.summary: An essay on autonomous AI agents and inference. The reading lead invites examination of assumptions and evidence; it is not an empirical endorsement of the essay’s conclusions.

posts.title: Epiplexity (epistemic complexity)
posts.summary: A research lead about learnable structure for computationally bounded observers, with a paper, code and lecture. Epiplexity is not silently equated with Shannon entropy or an established general systems law.

posts.title: Steven Hertzberg on LinkedIn – ‘AI research has rediscovered the Macy Conferences, and again without any attribution’
posts.summary: Steven Hertzberg’s commentary raises an attribution question about AI research and the Macy conferences. The allegation is recorded as commentary and does not establish either borrowing or an intellectual lineage.

posts.title: Where are the systems in ‘systems leadership’?  Leaderism, personal development, and the work of changing systems – Taylor (2026)
posts.summary: Benjamin P Taylor questions how systems leadership relates to changing the conditions that generate outcomes. The original essay is the canonical reading source; agreement or demonstrated effectiveness is not inferred.

posts.title: Bernhard Sterchi – Complexity Theory and Neo-Kantian Theory of Science – Tuesday, Oct 20 · 5:00pm UK time, The Complexity Lounge, online
posts.summary: An online Complexity Lounge talk by Bernhard Sterchi comparing complexity theory and Neo-Kantian approaches to science. The organiser’s event page provides the current booking and timing details.

posts.title: Hezen 2.0 – Treister (2009-2011) | cybernetic tarot
posts.summary: Suzanne Treister’s HEXEN 2.0 artwork brings cybernetic histories into a tarot-based artistic exploration. It is recorded as an attributed art and interpretation resource, not a validated divination or historical method.

limits: Published discovery records and source links, not full-text validation of every linked claim. Seven announcements reuse existing TNT resources. Original destinations remain canonical; SysCoI remains discovery provenance.
